claims.text: 10 Downing Street serves as the official London residence and executive office of the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The famous building is actually made up of three separate original properties: a mansion overlooking the park, a town house, and a small cottage.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The street itself was developed between 1682 and 1684 by Sir George Downing, who was notably a former spy for Oliver Cromwell.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Downing hired the legendary architect Christopher Wren to design the houses, but they were built so cheaply on soft soil that they suffered from shallow foundations.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: King George II first presented the property to Sir Robert Walpole, widely considered the first Prime Minister, in 1732.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The oldest part of the complex, known as the 'House at the Back', dates to 1530 and once secretly hosted early cabinet meetings after the Glorious Revolution of 1688.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Thomas Knyvet, who famously captured Guy Fawkes during the Gunpowder Plot in 1605, was once a resident of the 'House at the Back'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1985, Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher described the iconic building as 'one of the most precious jewels in the national heritage'.
claims.subject: self
